value.measure: Change in Central Rater Montgomery-Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) Total Score From Baseline to Post-dose Day 43

primary_endpoint.quote: Primary outcome: Change in Central Rater Montgomery-Asberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) Total Score From Baseline to Post-dose Day 43. The MADRS is a clinician-rated scale designed to measure depression severity and to detect changes due to antidepressant treatment. The scale consists of 10 items, each of which is scored from 0 (item not present or normal) to 6 (severe or continuous presence of the symptoms), for a total score range of 0-60. Higher scores represent a more severe condition. The total (composite) MADRS score is used as the endpoint. Time frame: Baseline; Day 43 post-dose

warnings: A blinding assessment was planned but no result was found: possible selective reporting.
Calibration is SYNTHETIC. Numbers demonstrate the method only; they are not real-world estimates.
limitations: Reverse causation: patients who improve may guess 'drug' because they improved. The correction then removes some real effect, so the corrected value is best read as a conservative bound, not the true effect.
Cross-trial confounding: trials with better blinding may differ in drug, dose, population or era.
A low-dose comparator is also pharmacology: a smaller gap mixes better blinding with real dose-response.
Extrapolation: few trials sit near zero unblinding, so the intercept is least certain exactly where it matters.
The tool estimates expectancy contamination. It does not predict what a future trial will show.
